subject: general
question: Which of the following blood is called 'the giver of all'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**O.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Although those with the **blood type O** are frequently referred to as **universal blood donors**, those with the blood type** O- (negative) **are the actual universal donors.
 
• It is as a result of the absence of **antigens **in their **red blood cells.**
 
• They are therefore able to **donate blood **to any other **blood group**.
 
• Blood cannot be **donated **to a** Rh-negative **person by a person with blood group **O+ (positive cells).**
 
• Due to its importance in emergencies, blood of **type O (positive and negative)** is in great demand.
 
• However, it is a common blood group because only** 7%** of people have the O-negative blood type and** 37%** of people have the **O-positive **blood type. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Antigens **in the blood are present or absent depending on the **blood group**.
 
• When a **foreign body **enters the **bloodstream**, the antigen helps the **immune system **respond by producing **antibodies **to combat it.
 
• **Red blood cells, white blood cells, **and **platelets** are all found in the **blood's plasma**, which is a liquid.
 
• The **four **major **blood types **are determined by the presence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs.
 
• In addition, whether a protein called the **Rh factor **is **present **or **absent **influences whether your blood group is **positive **or **negative**.
 
• The blood type can be **A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O-, AB+, or AB-** depending on certain variables.
